findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed one live, fast-moving juvenile cockroach near the back door of the facility.

The inspector recommends placing dated glue traps throughout the facility to track pest movement. Tracking is useful to better inform your pest control professional of pest location and number. An additional follow-up will be conducted on September 30, 2026 to monitor progress.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation 

Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets in the kitchen to read 0ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed and all buckets in the facility were replaced, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure the buckets are monitored with test strips to prevent inadequate sanitization of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the dish machine at the bar measure 0ppm chlorine after multiple attempts to troubleshoot the machine. The PIC was informed and plans to contact MJK for repair. In the meantime, all dishes from the bar must be sanitized in the kitchen dish machine until the bar machine is repaired. A follow-up will be conducted on August 4, 2026 for dish machine repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed all three soda nozzles at the bar to be soiled with black microbial growth. The PIC was informed of the soil. The nozzles are considered a food-contact surface, and therefore must be kept clean to sight and touch at all times. The nozzles were removed and sanitized during today’s visit. Ensure all food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation
Inspector observed the following items to be stored beyond its 7-day date mark:
1. Pork (expired July 22)
2. Beef x2 (expired July 18)
3. Chicken x2 (expired 7/22)
4. Ground beef x3 (expired July 28)
5. Beans x2 (expired July 28)
6. Beans x2 (expired July 22)

There were also multiple other containers with expired date marks that the inspector could not easily access due to stacking. The PIC was made aware that all items past the date mark must be discarded. A follow-up will be conducted on August 4, 2026 to ensure that proper date marking guidelines are being followed in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed 1 live roach crawling on a prep table between the walk-in cooler and cook line. The PIC was informed and plans to contact Orkin for service. Ensure receipts of this treatment is maintained on file for the inspector to view. 

A follow-up is scheduled for August 31, 2026 to ensure pest presence is reduced. Continue to have Orkin treat the facility and retain all receipts.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed food items and single-service items to be stored directly on the floor in the walk-in cooler, walk-in freezer, and the dry storage room connected to the walk-in cooler. Ensure food items are stored at least 6 inches off the ground to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no quaternary ammonia test strips available in the facility. There were chlorine test strips available for testing the dish machine, but a quaternary ammonia sanitizer dispenser is used for filling all sanitizer buckets. Ensure test strips of both varieties are available at all times for proper testing. A follow-up will be conducted on August 10, 2026 for test strip availability.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
2nd Repeat Violation.

The floor of the walk in freezer was observed with chunks of ice build up. Ensure that the freezer floor is maintained as often as necessary to prevent ice accumulation. Repairs may be necessary on the cooling unit of the freezer to prevent dripping.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following facility items in need of repair:
1. The ceiling light above the right side of the cook line is broken and exposing the bulbs. This poses a glass contamination hazard if the bulb were to break.
2. The shelves in the walk-in cooler were observed damaged and rusted. Rust can impart contaminates into food stored on the shelves. Ensure these shelves are sealed or replaced. 

Ensure these facility repairs are completed prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a hand sink to be missing paper towels. A reusable cloth was placed atop the paper towel dispenser. An employee stated that the cloth was in use as a replacement. Education was conducted regarding proper hand washing practices. Ensure disposable paper towels are used at all times to prevent cross-contamination. Never use reusable towels for drying clean hands. The hand sink was properly supplied during the inspection.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed reduced-oxygen packaged (ROP) salmon to be thawed in its original packaging. ROP fish must be removed from its original packaging prior to thawing to prevent the growth of Clostridium botulinum (the bacteria that produces the botulism toxin). A follow-up will be conducted on May 4, 2026 to ensure the salmon is removed from its original packaging prior to thawing.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.comment: An employee was observed handling a cellular device in the dish room. The employee the reached to handle clean dishes without washing hands. The activity was ceased and the employee was instructed to wash hands before handling clean dishes. Ensure to educate employees on proper phone usage and when to wash hands when contamination occurs.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The dish machine in the dish room was tested at 0ppm CL. The dish machine was cycled several times before contacting a technician to service the machine. A tube was replaced on the dish machine during the inspection and tested again at 100ppm CL to correct the violation. Ensure that chemical sanitizing dish machines test at the manufacturer's recommended concentration to be sure that dishes are getting sanitized properly. 

Also, the sanitizer bucket along the cookline was tested at 0ppm (Quat). Discussed with PIC and the bucket was recreated and tested at 200ppm (quat). Ensure that chemical sanitizers are maintained to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
There wasn't any paper towels at the hand-sink in the bar area or the hand-sink across from the cook line. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided. Ensure that paper towels are available at every hand-sink to wash hands properly. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed there to be no hand soap at the hand-sink in the bar area. Discussed with PIC and hand soap was provided. Ensure that handsoap is available at every handsink in order to properly wash hands. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the hand-sink across from the cook-line to be obstructed by a container. The container was removed by the owner. Ensure that hand-sinks are readily available for employees to wash hands and that they are never obstructed. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine’s (in kitchen) sanitizing concentration was tested at 0ppm (CL). An employee switched out the sanitizer bucket to correct the violation. The machine was tested again at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that the dish machine is testing at the manufacturer’s recommended sanitizing concentration to properly sanitize dishes. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed several containers of salsa stored in the line cooler to have temperatures between 58F-62F (probed). The cold unit was reset by the owner and the ambient temperature started to drop. An employee stated that the salsas were prepared about 2 hours prior to the inspection. Ice was added to the unit to lower the temperature. The salsa is made from canned tomatoes and is normally cold held after preparation. Be sure that TCS food items are held at 41F or below to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
A line cooler in the kitchen was observed to not be functioning properly. The cooler’s ambient temperatures were between (58F-62F). The cold unit was reset by the owner and the ambient temperature started to drop. Ice was added to the unit to lower the temperature quicker. The cooler’s ambient temperature was again recorded at 36F. Ensure that cold holding equipment is maintained and capable of holding cold food at 41F or below.  

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
A scoop stored in the sugar container was observed with the handle touching the sugar. Discussed with PIC and the scoop was taken to the dish machine to be cleaned. Ensure that utensils are always stored in a manner where the handle isn't in direct contact with the food to protect against contamination. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
(REPEAT X3) There was no certified food protection manager present during the inspection. Ensure that a CFPM is present to cover all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
The facility could not locate their employee reporting forms. Provided blank copies of employee reporting forms(in English and Spanish) for employees to sign and complete. Ensure that signed employee reporting forms are easily accessible for further routine inspections. 

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine in the outside bar area to have a sanitizing concentration of 0ppm (CL). Discussed with PIC and the sanitizer bottle was replaced. The sanitizing concentration was tested again at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that the dish machine’s sanitizer is maintained at the recommended concentration to properly sanitize dishes. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Observed a container of eggs stored in a drawer cooler along the cookline to be between 81F-87F. PIC noted that the eggs were boiled in the morning and placed in the cooler to cool down. Discussed with PIC alternative techniques to quickly cool eggs. The eggs were discarded by PIC. Ensure that eggs are being cooled properly and are never out of temperature for long periods of time. 

3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed a gallon of whole milk to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date in the kitchen’s dessert prep cooler. Discussed with PIC and milk was pulled and discarded. Ensure that milks stored in house over 24 hours never exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date.  

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the vent covers of the walk in cooler to be heavily soiled with debris. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that vent covers are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil buildup. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.comment:
Observed the handwashing sink across from the cookline to not have hot water. Owner is aware that the handsink lacks hot water and has been working to get the issue resolved. Ensure that handwashing sinks always have an adequate flow of running hot water to wash hands properly. 

5-103.12: Water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, EQUIPMENT, and nonFOOD EQUIPMENT that are required to use water except that water (A) and (B) to a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT or in response to a temporary interruption of a water supply need not be under pressure.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed an opened can of Pepsi mixed with food items intended for public consumption to be stored in a prep cooler along the cook-line. Discussed with PIC and the Pepsi was discarded. Ensure that personal items are always stored separate from food and drinks that will be served to the public. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Facility is not allergen trained. Ensure that at least one employee is allergen trained and can show proof of certification for future routine inspections. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.
